statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across four representative commerce templates plus login and failure-state probes.

page.framework: Server-rendered MPA with React-like search/category modules and legacy merchant templates
page.notes: The requested host root redirects to https://www.rakuten.co.jp/category/. Coverage includes the redirected category index, search results, a category template and one product detail.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance to the default capture; the reduced-motion/media probe reports color-scheme: normal and a light body background rgb(247,247,247), with no prefers-color-scheme rules.
Computed animation probe under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce found zero active animations; no reduced-motion-dependent motion remained to suppress.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using search-high-contrast.png, search-lighthouse-summary.json, product-lighthouse-summary.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: The preference probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules, while Lighthouse found multiple essential text contrast failures on both search and product templates.
The CSS/media feature probe found no view-transition rules and the MPA search-to-product journey performs a full abrupt navigation.
The audited templates contain no parallax, scrollytelling, reveal, or other scroll-linked motion to implement.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited templates contain no parallax, scrollytelling, reveal, or other scroll-linked motion to implement.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The result pages retain native browser scrolling and the DOM/CSS probe found no custom gesture surface fighting platform scrolling.
The search template is 10,403 CSS px tall, but the CSS feature probe found no scroll-state query or progress treatment and the captured header remains static.
No tooltip, transient popover, or viewport-edge menu was present in the exercised shopping path.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip, transient popover, or viewport-edge menu was present in the exercised shopping path.

checkOutcomes.method: visual journey and DOM link review
checkOutcomes.evidence: Breadcrumbs, explicit query/result text, visible filters and descriptive product links preserve location and next-action context.
Load screenshots across four templates showed no modal, consent wall or full-viewport interstitial obscuring core content.
No modal or transient overlay was presented during the exercised search and product journey.
checkOutcomes.reason: No modal or transient overlay was presented during the exercised search and product journey.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Desktop and mobile captures show multiple bright campaign banners, utility rows, notices and dense controls before or around the first product; the product capture devotes several viewports to store graphics.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using search-mobile.png, search-mobile-layout.json, category-mobile-layout.json, product-mobile.png
checkOutcomes.evidence: At a 360x800 viewport, search and category layouts report scrollWidth 1024 versus clientWidth 360, or 664 px overflow; index and product omit viewport metadata and are scaled-down desktop pages.
The search DOM reports body width 1024px and container-type: normal; the feature probe found no @container usage, and the narrow screenshot clips the product region.
The active DOM probe measured 436 of the first 500 visible links, buttons, and fields below 44px in at least one dimension; Lighthouse also failed target-size.
The entry identifies a category index; the search page shows the query, result count, filters and product links; the product page exposes price/product content.
A GET search for 米 returned product results and a result link successfully opened the representative product detail without an account wall.
A deliberately invalid route returned a clear 404 title, explanation, reload/back advice and a service-list recovery link.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using search-lighthouse-summary.json, product-lighthouse-summary.json, search-trace-summary.json, product-trace-summary.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured search LCP 10.3s, CLS 0.158 and TBT 1,400ms; product LCP was 21.9s, CLS 0.545 and TBT 870ms. CDP traces corroborated LCP of 6.34s and 19.27s.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using product-lighthouse-summary.json, index-mobile-layout.json, search-images.json, product-images.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.545 on the product page and 0.158 on search; the index layout observer recorded CLS 0.459. Image evidence found 46 dimensionless search images and 62 on product.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using search-trace-summary.json, search-summary.json, product-summary.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: Search Lighthouse reported 1,400ms TBT and the trace found three long tasks up to 377ms; the page loads 100 scripts. Product loads 167 scripts.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using search-summary.json, product-summary.json, search.har, product.har
checkOutcomes.evidence: HAR captured 372 requests/5.71MB for search and 499 requests/9.58MB for product, including parser-inserted high-priority styles/scripts; the product document took about 10.9s in the HAR.
Search transfers 4.15MB across 100 scripts; product transfers 4.18MB across 167. Search downloads repeated ~154KB Google tags and multiple ~151KB Facebook configurations.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using search-lighthouse-summary.json, product-lighthouse-summary.json, product-images.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scores were 0.62/0.69. Search failed aria-command-name with 54 nodes and invalid ARIA on 21; product images audit found 63 images without alt and Lighthouse found unlabeled controls.
Lighthouse failed color-contrast on both templates; product has 12 groups including #f2ab00 on white at 1.98:1 and #8f8f8f on white at 3.23:1.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using search-document-probe.json, category-document-probe.json, product-document-probe.json, search-lighthouse-summary.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: Search, category and product probes found no h1; search had only one landmark and product had none. Lighthouse failed landmark-one-main and found focusable descendants inside aria-hidden search carousel slides.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using index-mobile.png, product-mobile.png, search-dom.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: The 360px index and product screenshots shrink 1024–1244px canvases into the viewport; search body text is 12px and clipped horizontally.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using search-mobile-layout.json, category-mobile-layout.json, product-document-probe.json, search-lighthouse-summary.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: Search/category retain 664px horizontal overflow at 360px; index/product have no viewport meta, and Lighthouse failed meta-viewport/target-size checks.
Lighthouse recorded 17 console errors on search and 22 on product, dominated by failed/CORS-blocked Yahoo analytics calls.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using search-images.json, product-images.json, product-lighthouse-summary.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: Image probes found 46 search and 62 product images without dimensions; product Lighthouse failed image-aspect-ratio and 85 of 87 inspected images use legacy formats.
Both Lighthouse runs report deprecated Attribution Reporting use from Google tags and fail BFCache/inspector checks; product also has a broken source-map warning.
All four templates returned descriptive titles and meta descriptions; search title is “【楽天市場】米の通販”.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using product-document-probe.json, index-mobile-layout.json, search-mobile-layout.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: Although links are mostly real hrefs and raw HTML is strong, the entry/product pages omit viewport metadata and representative narrow layouts fail reflow.
Representative public pages returned HTTP 200 with canonical URLs and no accidental noindex; robots.txt allows the audited search route.
The inspected product exposes BreadcrumbList JSON-LD and complete Open Graph tags but no Product JSON-LD, despite being a commercial product entity. Search exposes only og:image among OG tags.
HTTPS, HSTS and nosniff are present, but CSP only contains frame-ancestors; 18 first-party cookies were flagged, with many not Secure and SameSite=None.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using search-trackers.json, product-trackers.json, search-summary.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: Tracker capture found 58 third-party origins and 14 known tracker domains on search; HAR attributes 370 of 372 requests and 5.62MB to non-main-origin hosts. Product reaches 77 third-party origins.

checkOutcomes.method: load walkthrough and central login DOM probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: No permission prompt appeared on load. The central login form uses autocomplete=username and its source contains passkey affordances.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using search-headers.json, search-lighthouse-summary.json, product-lighthouse-summary.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: Permissions-Policy is missing, CSP lacks script/style/default restrictions, and Lighthouse observed 54–55 third-party cookies across the representative pages.

checkOutcomes.method: discoverability raw HTML versus rendered DOM
checkOutcomes.evidence: Raw-HTML coverage was 63% on the entry and 80–91% on search/category/product; all were non-shell pages with core text present without JS.

checkOutcomes.method: screenshots, HAR failures and journey review
checkOutcomes.evidence: The exercised listing/product pages loaded usable content despite several failed tracker requests; no clipped transient overlay blocked the path.
This transaction/search marketplace intrinsically depends on live inventory, pricing and account services; installability/offline transaction support is not expected.
checkOutcomes.reason: This transaction/search marketplace intrinsically depends on live inventory, pricing and account services; installability/offline transaction support is not expected.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The invalid route rendered a useful 404 with explanation and recovery links rather than a blank shell.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM html lang and visual reading-order review
checkOutcomes.evidence: Representative documents declare lang=ja; Japanese left-to-right content and reading order render consistently on inspected pages.
Prices render as Japanese yen and delivery/calendar dates use Japanese locale conventions throughout the representative commerce path.
The audited search and product path contains local delivery dates but no user-created global event or recurring time-zone-sensitive schedule.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited search and product path contains local delivery dates but no user-created global event or recurring time-zone-sensitive schedule.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The inspected pages disclose product prices, shipping caveats, result ordering and deadlines; no consent wall, confirmshaming or forced continuity appeared.
Search inputs are optional and the tested invalid route gives neutral, actionable recovery guidance without blaming the user.

checkOutcomes.method: login and search form DOM probes
checkOutcomes.evidence: The relevant account identifier field uses autocomplete=username and is programmatically labelled; search fields do not collect address/payment credentials.
The product/search surfaces visibly disclose price, shipping variability and delivery caveats; account sign-in is delegated to a clearly labelled central flow with passkey strings present.
Product transfers 5.08MB of images; 85 of 87 inspected product images use legacy formats, 78 below-fold images are not lazy, 51 lack srcset, and 62 lack dimensions.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence using search-summary.json, search-trackers.json, search-trace-summary.json
checkOutcomes.evidence: Search makes 372 requests including 72 fetch/XHR and 100 scripts; trackers include multiple repeated pixels/tags and failed requests that still consume CPU/network.
Search transfers 5.71MB with 5.62MB attributed outside the main origin; product transfers 9.58MB and loads 498 of 499 requests from other origins, including 5.08MB images.
No declared intent indicates an agent-facing surface; this emerging capability is not required for the current human shopping scope.
checkOutcomes.reason: No declared intent indicates an agent-facing surface; this emerging capability is not required for the current human shopping scope.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No declared product intent calls for summarisation or on-device inference in the audited shopping path.
checkOutcomes.reason: No declared product intent calls for summarisation or on-device inference in the audited shopping path.

checkOutcomes.method: repeated-scroll metrics and baseline/post heap summaries
checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten full-page scroll down/up cycles, same-session DOM nodes remained 6,501 and used JS heap fell from 130.7MB to 97.4MB; separate heap summaries differed only 1.31%.

The heap summary reported about 115.5MB self size, 2.21M heap nodes and 11.75M edges after load. Repeated scrolling did not indicate a leak, but the cold footprint is disproportionate and aligns with 100 scripts.
The repeated scroll probe kept DOM node count fixed at 6,501 and showed no monotonic used-heap growth; no leak signal was established.

principleOutcomes.reason: No declared intent indicates an agent-facing surface; this emerging capability is not required for the current human shopping scope. No declared product intent calls for summarisation or on-device inference in the audited shopping path.

paths.description: Requested entry URL and redirected global category-index archetype.
Primary search journey and dense results/filter template using query 米.
Representative category/ranking template for women’s fashion.
Representative product detail and commercial decision surface reached from search.
Central account sign-in entry inspected for labels, autocomplete and modern authentication signals; no credentials entered.
Deliberately invalid route inspected for HTTP/error recovery UX.

findings.summary: The shopping surfaces ignore the user’s dark-theme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance to the default capture; the reduced-motion/media probe reports color-scheme: normal and a light body background rgb(247,247,247), with no prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide tested dark tokens through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: No preference-specific high-contrast treatment is provided.
findings.evidence: The preference probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules, while Lighthouse found multiple essential text contrast failures on both search and product templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations, preserve system colors, and retest controls and status text.

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt and do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS/media feature probe found no view-transition rules and the MPA search-to-product journey performs a full abrupt navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin listing-to-detail navigation, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long result pages provide no scroll-state feedback.
findings.evidence: The search template is 10,403 CSS px tall, but the CSS feature probe found no scroll-state query or progress treatment and the captured header remains static.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll-state-aware compact header or progress/return affordance without obscuring results.

findings.summary: Promotional chrome competes with the primary shopping content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile captures show multiple bright campaign banners, utility rows, notices and dense controls before or around the first product; the product capture devotes several viewports to store graphics.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce stacked promotional banners and collapse secondary chrome so query, filters, products, price and purchase actions dominate.

findings.summary: Core templates render a fixed desktop canvas on mobile.
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 viewport, search and category layouts report scrollWidth 1024 versus clientWidth 360, or 664 px overflow; index and product omit viewport metadata and are scaled-down desktop pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt a real mobile viewport, fluid/intrinsic layout, and responsive product/detail templates with no horizontal overflow.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: The search DOM reports body width 1024px and container-type: normal; the feature probe found no @container usage, and the narrow screenshot clips the product region.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace fixed-width shells with container-query components and intrinsic grids that reflow filters and result cards.

findings.summary: Most interactive targets are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: The active DOM probe measured 436 of the first 500 visible links, buttons, and fields below 44px in at least one dimension; Lighthouse also failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Use at least 44x44 CSS px target boxes, spacing between adjacent controls, and clearly visible :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: Representative pages miss the Core Web Vitals performance bar by a wide margin.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured search LCP 10.3s, CLS 0.158 and TBT 1,400ms; product LCP was 21.9s, CLS 0.545 and TBT 870ms. CDP traces corroborated LCP of 6.34s and 19.27s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, cut startup JavaScript/trackers, reserve space, and establish enforceable per-template performance budgets.

findings.summary: Late content causes severe layout movement.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.545 on the product page and 0.158 on search; the index layout observer recorded CLS 0.459. Image evidence found 46 dimensionless search images and 62 on product.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image/banner/ad slots with dimensions or aspect-ratio and prevent late campaign modules from moving existing content.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: Search Lighthouse reported 1,400ms TBT and the trace found three long tasks up to 377ms; the page loads 100 scripts. Product loads 167 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove nonessential startup code, split long tasks, and schedule analytics and recommendations after core interaction readiness.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is extremely heavy and has long critical chains.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 372 requests/5.71MB for search and 499 requests/9.58MB for product, including parser-inserted high-priority styles/scripts; the product document took about 10.9s in the HAR.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten parser-blocking chains, consolidate critical CSS, defer scripts, improve document latency, caching, and image priority.

findings.summary: Third-party and duplicate script payload dominates the load.
findings.evidence: Search transfers 4.15MB across 100 scripts; product transfers 4.18MB across 167. Search downloads repeated ~154KB Google tags and multiple ~151KB Facebook configurations.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory tags, deduplicate vendor instances, conditionally load advertising integrations, and remove unused JavaScript/CSS.

findings.summary: Interactive controls and media lack accessible names and valid roles.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scores were 0.62/0.69. Search failed aria-command-name with 54 nodes and invalid ARIA on 21; product images audit found 63 images without alt and Lighthouse found unlabeled controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native controls, valid ARIA only when needed, programmatic labels, meaningful alt text, and hide decorative images.

findings.summary: Essential text fails WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed color-contrast on both templates; product has 12 groups including #f2ab00 on white at 1.98:1 and #8f8f8f on white at 3.23:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Update text/status tokens to meet 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text/UI, then regression-test.

findings.summary: Document structure and focus semantics are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Search, category and product probes found no h1; search had only one landmark and product had none. Lighthouse failed landmark-one-main and found focusable descendants inside aria-hidden search carousel slides.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a single descriptive h1, main/nav landmarks, logical headings, and remove hidden carousel descendants from the tab order.

findings.summary: Scaled desktop layouts make text cramped and illegible on narrow screens.
findings.evidence: The 360px index and product screenshots shrink 1024–1244px canvases into the viewport; search body text is 12px and clipped horizontally.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive typography with readable minimum sizes, sensible line lengths, and reflow instead of page-scale shrinking.

findings.summary: The experience fails mobile reflow and target-size requirements.
findings.evidence: Search/category retain 664px horizontal overflow at 360px; index/product have no viewport meta, and Lighthouse failed meta-viewport/target-size checks.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide scalable viewport metadata, 320px reflow without two-dimensional scrolling, and adequately sized touch targets.

findings.summary: Third-party integrations log many browser errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded 17 console errors on search and 22 on product, dominated by failed/CORS-blocked Yahoo analytics calls.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix or remove failing integrations and gate optional analytics so normal page loads produce no console errors.

findings.summary: Images are frequently unsized, unlabeled, or use problematic aspect handling.
findings.evidence: Image probes found 46 search and 62 product images without dimensions; product Lighthouse failed image-aspect-ratio and 85 of 87 inspected images use legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, preserve source aspect ratios, and standardise responsive image markup.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and browser lifecycle blockers remain.
findings.evidence: Both Lighthouse runs report deprecated Attribution Reporting use from Google tags and fail BFCache/inspector checks; product also has a broken source-map warning.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or remove deprecated vendor integrations, resolve inspector issues and audit BFCache blockers/source maps.

findings.summary: Public pages are not consistently mobile friendly.
findings.evidence: Although links are mostly real hrefs and raw HTML is strong, the entry/product pages omit viewport metadata and representative narrow layouts fail reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add viewport metadata and responsive templates while preserving the existing server-rendered crawlable links.

findings.summary: Product structured data is incomplete.
findings.evidence: The inspected product exposes BreadcrumbList JSON-LD and complete Open Graph tags but no Product JSON-LD, despite being a commercial product entity. Search exposes only og:image among OG tags.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Product/Offer/AggregateRating JSON-LD and complete share metadata that matches visible price, availability, image and title.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP protections are weaker than the HTTPS transport suggests.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS and nosniff are present, but CSP only contains frame-ancestors; 18 first-party cookies were flagged, with many not Secure and SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a full nonce/hash-based CSP and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest SameSite and HttpOnly settings appropriate to purpose.

findings.summary: The page sends a very large tracking footprint on first load.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 58 third-party origins and 14 known tracker domains on search; HAR attributes 370 of 372 requests and 5.62MB to non-main-origin hosts. Product reaches 77 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise vendors, load consent-dependent tags only after a valid choice, batch necessary analytics, and proxy/partition first-party assets separately from trackers.

findings.summary: Defensive policy coverage is incomplete and third-party cookie dependence is high.
findings.evidence: Permissions-Policy is missing, CSP lacks script/style/default restrictions, and Lighthouse observed 54–55 third-party cookies across the representative pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy Permissions-Policy and a complete CSP; reduce third-party cookie dependence and verify frame, referrer and origin-isolation posture.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bandwidth.
findings.evidence: Product transfers 5.08MB of images; 85 of 87 inspected product images use legacy formats, 78 below-fold images are not lazy, 51 lack srcset, and 62 lack dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold media, and enforce dimensions and per-image byte budgets.

findings.summary: Background advertising and analytics perform disproportionate work.
findings.evidence: Search makes 372 requests including 72 fetch/XHR and 100 scripts; trackers include multiple repeated pixels/tags and failed requests that still consume CPU/network.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant pixels, defer nonessential background work, batch events, and stop retries/requests that fail or add no user value.

findings.summary: Third-party and media weight is disproportionate to the shopping task.
findings.evidence: Search transfers 5.71MB with 5.62MB attributed outside the main origin; product transfers 9.58MB and loads 498 of 499 requests from other origins, including 5.08MB images.
findings.suggestedFix: Set third-party, script, image and request-count budgets; block releases that exceed them and defer optional media/tags.

findings.summary: The initial heap footprint is high for a result listing.
findings.evidence: The heap summary reported about 115.5MB self size, 2.21M heap nodes and 11.75M edges after load. Repeated scrolling did not indicate a leak, but the cold footprint is disproportionate and aligns with 100 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce shipped/runtime code and object graphs, virtualise long lists where useful, and track heap/node budgets in representative sessions.

taskList.title: Ship genuinely responsive search, category and product templates
Cut LCP, blocking work and network weight with strict template budgets
Reduce and consent-gate the tracking footprint; harden cookies and CSP
Fix accessible names, roles, landmarks, focus and contrast
Reserve media space and modernise responsive image delivery
Reduce promotional chrome and restore content hierarchy
Add user-preference theming and modern route transitions
Complete product structured metadata and platform hygiene
